```{r setup, include = FALSE}
fs <- q$food

applicants <- sum(a$status == "Applied")
requested <- sum(a$requested, na.rm = TRUE)
flat_each <- param(p, "Flat per on-time applicant")
flex_pool <- param(p, "Flexible pool")
food_cap <- param(p, "Programmatic food cap")
social_cap <- param(p, "Social event HSG ceiling")
w_stew <- param(p, "Weight: Financial Stewardship")
w_collab <- param(p, "Weight: Collaboration")
w_impact <- param(p, "Weight: Impact")
notes_file <- file.path("notes", paste0(quarter, ".md"))
```

### *`r quarter`*

## At a glance

<div class="callouts">
  <div class="callout">Budget<br><span class="callout-text">`r dollars(budget)`</span></div>
  <div class="callout">Allocated<br><span class="callout-text">`r dollars(allocated)`</span></div>
  <div class="callout">Total requested<br><span class="callout-text">`r dollars(requested)`</span></div>
  <div class="callout">HSOs that applied<br><span class="callout-text">`r applicants`</span></div>
  <div class="callout">Events reviewed<br><span class="callout-text">`r sum(fs$events)`</span></div>
</div>

The Finance Committee of Harris Student Government (HSG) allocates funding to Harris Student Organizations (HSOs) each quarter. This report shows what every HSO asked for, what it received, and why, so any student can check the decisions. Requests this quarter totaled `r dollars(requested)` against a `r dollars(budget)` budget, so the committee could fund about `r percent(allocated / requested)` of what was asked.`r if (budget - allocated > 0) paste0(' The remaining ', dollars(budget - allocated), ' goes to the Emergency Reserve, which is set aside for HSOs, including new HSOs that form during the year.') else ''`

## Our approach

The HSG Finance Committee exists to help HSOs turn the diversity, curiosity, and creativity of the Keller Center into real impact. That includes culture, art, and civic engagement. Policy doesn't happen in a vacuum. It grows out of how we work, study, and celebrate together.

Each committee member reviews roughly 120 events per quarter, and we evaluate every one on its merits. Some judgment is unavoidable, so we want to be clear about what we weigh:

* **Who it serves:** the specific community the event is designed for
* **What it aims to achieve:** its intended outcomes for that community
* **Why it matters:** how meaningfully it serves the people it's built for

We score impact holistically, not by size alone. Events designed for smaller communities are valued just as much as large ones when they serve their audience well.

Our goal is to channel that creativity into tangible benefits for Harris students today and to build an open, curious, evidence-driven culture that carries forward to future cohorts.

## How funding works

Every allocation has two parts:

* **Flat share:** 25% of the budget is split equally among every HSO that applied on time, `r dollars(flat_each)` each this quarter.
* **Flexible share:** the remaining `r dollars(flex_pool)` is split in proportion to each HSO's **committee score × eligible request**.

**Eligible request** is what an HSO asked for, minus food spending above these limits:

| Event type | What it means | What HSG covers |
|---|---|---|
| Cultural | The food or cultural practice *is* the event | All food |
| Programmatic | A speaker, panel, training or service event that would happen without food | Food up to `r percent(food_cap)` of the event budget |
| Social | The gathering itself is the point (mixers, pub nights, outings) | Up to `r dollars(social_cap)` per event, times the number of confirmed co-hosting HSOs |

**Committee score** is the average of each reviewer's score plus one automatic score computed from the application. Every reviewer scores three areas from 1 to 5, weighted `r percent(w_stew)` Financial Stewardship, `r percent(w_collab)` Collaboration & Inclusion and `r percent(w_impact)` Impact. Reviewers recuse themselves from HSOs they belong to.

**Rollover** is each HSO's HarrisHub "Available" balance, and it counts toward the HSO's events. An HSO can set part of it aside as an earmark when the money is restricted by a sponsor, donor or grant, committed under a signed contract, or saved for a specific event later in the academic year that the HSO itemizes with its cost. General savings don't count.

See [METHODOLOGY.md](https://github.com/A-Sarkar18/hsg-finance-transparency/blob/main/METHODOLOGY.md) for a summary of the rules and formulas, and the [policy documents](https://github.com/A-Sarkar18/hsg-finance-transparency/tree/main/policy) for the full Fall 2026 policy.

No HSO can receive more than its flat share plus its eligible request, and allocations are rounded to the nearest $10. Any change the committee makes by hand is marked with a short note in the table at the end.

## Allocations

```{r}
ap <- filter(a, status == "Applied", requested > 0)
top5_share <- sum(head(sort(ap$requested, decreasing = TRUE), 5)) / sum(ap$requested)
```

A few large requests drive most of the demand: the five largest requests made up `r percent(top5_share)` of all money requested this quarter.

```{r, fig.height = 4}
plot_request_sizes(a)
```

Each HSO's request, eligible request and allocation, with the share of its request that was funded:

```{r, fig.height = 8}
plot_allocations(a)
```

## What drove the allocations

Higher-scoring applications tended to receive a larger share of their eligible request. Smaller requests also score higher on this measure, because the equal flat share is a bigger part of them.

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_score_share(a)
```

Rollover and outside funds lower an HSO's automatic Financial Stewardship score. The chart shows each HSO's balance relative to its request against the share it received.

```{r, fig.height = 5.5}
plot_rollover(a)
```

## Food and event rules

Of `r dollars(sum(fs$food))` in food requested across `r sum(fs$events)` events, `r dollars(sum(fs$excluded))` fell outside the limits above and was left out of eligible requests. HSOs can still spend on it, using rollover, RSO funds or sponsors.

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
plot_food(fs)
```

```{r, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(q$attendance)) {
  at <- q$attendance
  small <- sum(at$events[at$band %in% c("1-24", "25-49")])
  share <- small / sum(at$events)
  lead <- if (share > 0.55) "Most events" else if (share >= 0.45) "About half of all events" else "Many events"
  cat(lead, " (", small, " of ", sum(at$events), ") expect fewer than 50 people.\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
if (!is.null(q$attendance)) plot_attendance(q$attendance)
```

## FAQs

#### Who reviews my HSO's allocation application?

* **The HSG Finance Committee.** Five committee members each read every application and score the HSO from 1 to 5 in three areas: Financial Stewardship (`r percent(w_stew)`), Collaboration & Inclusion (`r percent(w_collab)`) and Impact (`r percent(w_impact)`).
* **An automatic score** calculated from the application data (rollover, collaborations, expected attendance) counts as one more reviewer.
* **Reviewers recuse themselves** from HSOs they belong to.
* **Scoring is by HSO, not by event.** Every event is still read and classified so the food rules can be applied.
* **The HSG Executive Board** then reviews and votes to approve each HSO's amount.
* **Full scoring criteria:** see the [policy documents](#policy-documents).

#### How is my allocation calculated?

* **Equal base share:** 25% of the budget is split equally among every HSO that applied on time (`r dollars(flat_each)` each this quarter).
* **Shared pool:** the other 75% is split in proportion to **committee score × eligible request**.
* **Eligible request** is what the HSO asked for, minus food spending above the limits described in [How funding works](#how-funding-works).
* **Upper limit and rounding:** no HSO gets more than its base share plus its eligible request, and amounts are rounded to the nearest $10.

#### Why did my HSO get less than it asked for?

* **Requests are bigger than the budget.** This quarter they totaled about `r round(requested / budget, 1)` times the budget, so every HSO received part of its request.
* **The biggest factors** are food spending above the limits, a large rollover balance compared with the request, and few co-hosted events.
* **The committee score** sets each HSO's share of the pool.

#### Will events for smaller communities, or events without co-hosts, score lower?

No. The automatic score is only one of six voices, and it can't see everything. It counts attendance and co-hosts, but it can't tell how much an event matters to the people it serves.

That's what the five human reviewers are for. They score Impact by **who an event serves and how well it serves them**, not by size alone. Events for historically underrepresented communities, and policy topics that matter deeply to a smaller group, are valued as much as large events. Not every good event needs a co-host, and reviewers take that into account too.

#### Does my rollover count against me?

* **Yes, by default.** We use each HSO's HarrisHub "Available" balance as rollover, and a large balance compared with the request lowers the Stewardship score.
* **Earmarked money is set aside** when the HSO documents it in its application: money restricted by a sponsor, donor or grant; money committed under a signed contract; or money saved for a specific, itemized event later in the same academic year, with its estimated cost and planned quarter.
* **General savings don't count**, including money saved for unspecified "future events" or for after the academic year ends.

#### Who decides when my HSO gets its allocation?

The process involves HSO leaders, HSG and SEB (Student Engagement and Belonging):

1. HSG emails HSO leaders when applications open.
2. HSO leaders submit the application on HarrisHub by the deadline.
3. The Finance Committee classifies every event and sends each HSO its event classifications.
4. **HSOs have 72 hours** to contest a classification, correct attendance, confirm co-hosts, update rollover or claim earmarked funds. **This is the only chance to appeal.**
5. The Finance Committee scores applications and sets allocation amounts.
6. The HSG Executive Board reviews and votes to approve each amount.
7. HSOs are emailed their final allocation amount. Amounts can't be changed after this point.
8. HSG sends SEB the approved amounts.
9. SEB adds the funds to each HSO's HarrisHub account.

#### When does each quarter's funding arrive?

| Quarter funded | Apply | Funds arrive |
|---|---|---|
| Fall | By June of the previous academic year | By week 2 of Fall |
| Winter | About week 7 of Fall | Week 1 of Winter |
| Spring | About week 7 of Winter | Week 1 of Spring |

HSOs always apply the quarter before. For Fall, that means applying before summer break so funds are ready when the year starts. HSG emails exact dates each quarter.

#### What if we miss the deadline?

Late applications aren't guaranteed a review. Any the committee accepts receive the equal base share only.

#### Is there a way to get my allocation sooner?

Not really. What helps is replying quickly to the Finance Committee's email confirming your amount: the sooner HSOs respond, the sooner HSG can send the amounts to SEB.

#### What happens to money that isn't allocated?

It goes to the Emergency Reserve, which is set aside for HSO use, including new HSOs that form during the year. This quarter, `r dollars(budget - allocated)` went to the reserve.

#### Where can I see every HSO's allocation?

Right here. The [appendix](#appendix-allocations-by-hso) lists what each HSO requested and received.

#### Who do I contact with questions?

Email the Finance Committee Chair, Ayan Sarkar.
